description: If the price of a good rises from $10 to $12 and quantity demanded falls from 200 to 160 units, what is the price elasticity of demand using the midpoint method?
hint: Midpoint PED = (% change Q) / (% change P) using averages as base
choice1: -1.22 (elastic)
choice3: -2.44 (elastic)
column15: -0.50 (inelastic)

description: A simultaneous increase in both supply and demand for a good will definitely result in:
explanation: When both supply and demand increase the equilibrium quantity rises because more is supplied and demanded. The price effect is ambiguous - it depends on the relative size of the shifts.
choice1: A higher equilibrium price and higher quantity
choice2: A lower equilibrium price and lower quantity
choice3: A higher equilibrium quantity with ambiguous price change
column15: A lower equilibrium quantity with ambiguous price change

description: A firm has total fixed costs of $500 and produces 100 units with total variable costs of $300. What is the average total cost?
If the marginal propensity to consume (MPC) is 0.8, what is the value of the fiscal multiplier?
explanation: The fiscal multiplier = 1 / (1 - MPC) = 1 / (1 - 0.8) = 1 / 0.2 = 5.

description: Country X can produce 20 tons of rice or 5 cars; Country Y can produce 15 tons of rice or 10 cars. Which country has comparative advantage in cars?
explanation: Country X opportunity cost per car = 20/5 = 4 tons of rice. Country Y opp. cost per car = 15/10 = 1.5 tons of rice. Y has lower opp. cost so Y has comparative advantage in cars.
choice1: Country X because it produces more rice
choice2: Country X because it produces fewer cars
choice3: Country Y because its opportunity cost per car is lower
column15: Neither; they have equal comparative advantage

description: The Fisher equation shows the relationship between nominal interest rates real interest rates and inflation. If the nominal rate is 7% and expected inflation is 3% what is the approximate real interest rate?
explanation: Fisher equation: real rate = nominal rate - inflation rate = 7% - 3% = 4%.
hint: Real rate = Nominal rate - Inflation rate

description: A profit-maximizing monopolist produces where MR = MC. If at that output level the price is $50 and ATC is $30 what is the per-unit economic profit?
explanation: Economic profit per unit = Price - ATC = $50 - $30 = $20 per unit.

description: Nominal GDP in Year 1 is $10 trillion and the GDP deflator is 125 (base year = 100). What is real GDP in Year 1?
explanation: Real GDP = (Nominal GDP / GDP Deflator) x 100 = (10 / 125) x 100 = $8 trillion.
choice1: $12.5 trillion
choice3: $10 trillion
column15: $15 trillion

description: A firm raises its price by 5% and total revenue falls. This means the price elasticity of demand is:
explanation: When total revenue falls after a price increase demand is elastic (PED magnitude > 1) because the quantity drop outweighs the price gain.
hint: TR falls after price rise means PED > 1 in magnitude
choice1: Inelastic (|PED| < 1)
choice3: Elastic (|PED| > 1)
column15: Perfectly inelastic (|PED| = 0)

description: When a consumer moves along an indifference curve from one bundle to another their:
explanation: An indifference curve shows combinations of goods giving equal utility. Moving along it keeps utility constant while the quantities of the two goods change.
choice1: Utility remains constant but the bundle changes
choice3: Marginal utility of both goods stays constant
column15: Budget line has shifted outward

description: If the government has a budget deficit and chooses to finance it by borrowing (issuing bonds) this can crowd out private investment by:
explanation: When the government borrows heavily it competes with private borrowers for loanable funds driving up interest rates which discourages private investment - the crowding out effect.
choice1: Lowering the tax burden on firms
choice3: Reducing consumer confidence immediately
column15: Raising interest rates which reduces private investment

description: Which of the following best describes the transmission mechanism from a central bank interest rate cut to GDP growth?
explanation: A rate cut lowers borrowing costs encouraging more investment and consumer spending which raises aggregate demand and ultimately increases real GDP.
choice1: Lower rates reduce inflation first then GDP falls
choice2: Lower rates encourage borrowing and spending raising aggregate demand and GDP
choice3: Lower rates cause currency appreciation reducing exports and GDP
column15: Lower rates lead to higher saving reducing consumption and GDP

description: In monopolistic competition in the long run economic profit is driven to zero because:
explanation: Easy entry attracts new competitors in response to profits. Competition reduces each firm's demand until price equals ATC and economic profit is zero.
choice1: The government sets price equal to average cost
choice2: Firms collude to keep prices low
choice3: Free entry of new firms erodes profits until P = ATC
column15: Consumers switch to substitute goods permanently

description: What happens in a market when the government imposes a binding price ceiling below the equilibrium price?
explanation: A binding price ceiling set below equilibrium keeps the price too low: quantity demanded exceeds quantity supplied creating a persistent shortage.
choice1: A shortage arises because Qd > Qs at the ceiling price
choice2: A surplus arises because Qs > Qd at the ceiling price
choice3: The market adjusts to a new equilibrium at the ceiling
column15: Both price and quantity rise above equilibrium

description: A firm produces 50 units with total cost $1,000. When it produces 51 units total cost rises to $1,025. What is the marginal cost of the 51st unit?
explanation: Marginal cost = change in total cost / change in quantity = (1025 - 1000) / (51 - 50) = $25.
hint: MC = change in TC / change in Q

description: If nominal GDP grows from $8 trillion to $9 trillion and the GDP deflator rises from 100 to 112.5, by approximately what percentage did real GDP grow?
explanation: Real GDP Year 1 = 8 trillion. Real GDP Year 2 = (9 / 112.5) x 100 = 8 trillion. Real GDP grew by 0%. All of nominal growth was due to inflation.
choice2: 0% - all growth was due to inflation
choice3: 12% real growth
column15: 8% real growth

description: A steel plant produces 100 tons of steel per day generating pollution that costs nearby residents $10 per ton. If the social optimum output is 80 tons per day an appropriate Pigouvian tax would be:
explanation: A Pigouvian tax should equal the marginal external cost per unit. The cost imposed on others is $10 per ton so a $10 per ton tax is needed to align private and social costs.
choice1: $80 per day total
choice3: $ 10 per ton
column15: $20 per ton

description: Country A has opportunity cost of 2 units of cloth per unit of wheat; Country B has opportunity cost of 3 units of cloth per unit of wheat. Which country has comparative advantage in wheat and what does this predict?
explanation: Country A gives up less cloth per wheat (2 vs. 3) so Country A has comparative advantage in wheat. Country B has comparative advantage in cloth.
choice1: Country A has comparative advantage in wheat; trade benefits both nations
choice2: Country B has comparative advantage in wheat; it should export wheat
choice3: Neither country should specialize; self-sufficiency is optimal
column15: Country A should produce both goods since it has lower opportunity cost in everything

description: If the economy is operating above its potential GDP output gap the most likely concern for policymakers is:
explanation: When actual output exceeds potential GDP resources are over-utilized. This creates upward wage and price pressures - the main risk is demand-pull inflation.
choice1: Rising structural unemployment
choice3: A rapid fall in the exchange rate
column15: Demand-pull inflation as resource utilization exceeds capacity

description: A 10% increase in the price of coffee leads to a 15% increase in the quantity demanded of tea. What is the cross-price elasticity of demand and what does it indicate?
explanation: Cross-price elasticity = % change in Qd of Tea / % change in Price of Coffee = 15% / 10% = +1.5. Positive cross-price elasticity means the goods are substitutes.
hint: Cross-price PED = % change Qd of Y / % change P of X
choice1: -1.5; the goods are complements
choice3: 0.67; the goods are complements
column15: 1.5; the goods are normal goods

description: The money multiplier is 1 / reserve requirement. If the required reserve ratio is 10% and the central bank injects $100 million into the banking system what is the maximum potential increase in the money supply?
explanation: Money multiplier = 1 / 0.10 = 10. Maximum increase = $100 million x 10 = $1
calculator: Money supply increase = injection x (1 / reserve ratio)
choice3: $100 million

description: Which of the following correctly describes the relationship between marginal cost and average variable cost curves?
explanation: When MC is below AVC it pulls AVC down; when MC is above AVC it pulls AVC up. MC crosses AVC at the minimum of the AVC curve.
hint: MC crosses AVC and ATC at their minimum points
choice1: MC intersects AVC at its minimum point
choice2: MC intersects AVC at its maximum point
choice3: MC is always above AVC
column15: MC is always equal to AVC

description: In a perfectly competitive industry the long-run equilibrium price equals:
explanation: In long-run perfectly competitive equilibrium free entry drives economic profit to zero. Price equals minimum average total cost and also equals marginal cost.
hint: P = MC = minimum ATC in long-run competitive equilibrium
choice1: Average fixed cost
choice3: Marginal revenue which exceeds price
column15: Minimum average total cost

description: When the income elasticity of demand for a good is negative the good is classified as:
explanation: Income elasticity of demand = % change in Qd / % change in income. A negative value means demand falls as income rises - the defining characteristic of an inferior good.
choice1: A normal good
choice3: A Giffen good only
column15: A luxury good

description: An import quota and a tariff both restrict trade but differ in that:
explanation: A tariff generates government revenue (like a tax) while a quota generates no revenue for the government - instead the gain goes to whoever holds the import licenses.
choice1: A quota raises revenue for the government while a tariff does not
choice2: A tariff limits quantities while a quota raises prices
choice3: A tariff generates revenue for the government while a quota typically does not
column15: A quota only applies to goods while a tariff only applies to services

description: Real GDP grows 3% and the population grows 1%. By approximately what percentage does real GDP per capita grow?
explanation: GDP per capita growth rate = GDP growth rate - population growth rate = 3% - 1% = 2%.
hint: GDP per capita growth = GDP growth - population growth

description: The substitution effect of a price increase refers to:
explanation: When a good's price rises it becomes relatively more expensive compared to substitutes. Holding real income constant consumers substitute away from it - this is the substitution effect.
choice1: The consumer buying more due to higher income
choice2: The shift in the budget constraint outward
choice3: Buying more of the good because it is now more valuable
column15: Switching to cheaper alternatives because the good became relatively more expensive

description: If the MPC is 0.75 and the government increases spending by $200 billion what is the total change in GDP predicted by the simple Keynesian multiplier?
explanation: Multiplier = 1 / (1 - 0.75) = 1 / 0.25 = 4. Change in GDP = 4 x $200 billion = $800 billion.
choice1: $200 billion
choice3: $150 billion

description: Negative externalities cause a market to produce:
explanation: Because the private cost is below the true social cost firms produce more than is socially optimal. The market quantity exceeds the efficient quantity.
hint: Private cost < Social cost means overproduction
choice1: Less than the socially optimal quantity
choice3: More than the socially optimal quantity
column15: The socially optimal quantity only if regulated

description: If income elasticity of demand for a good is 2.5 the good is best classified as:
explanation: Income elasticity > 1 means demand rises faster than income - this is the definition of a luxury good (also called an income-elastic or superior good).
choice1: A luxury good
choice3: An inferior good
column15: A Giffen good

description: If a central bank wants to reduce inflation it would most likely:
explanation: Raising interest rates reduces borrowing consumption and investment lowering aggregate demand and reducing upward pressure on prices.
choice1: Buy government bonds on the open market
choice3: Decrease the discount rate
column15: Raise the policy interest rate to reduce aggregate demand

description: A firm in an oligopoly considering a price change must account for:
explanation: In oligopoly firms are interdependent. Any firm changing its price must anticipate how rivals will respond - a key feature distinguishing oligopoly from perfect competition.
choice1: Government approval for every price change
choice2: Rivals' likely reactions to the price change
choice3: The infinite number of competitors in the market
column15: Fixed marginal costs across all firms

description: Using the income approach GDP equals the sum of:
explanation: The income approach to GDP measures all incomes earned in producing goods and services: wages (labor income) profits rents and interest.
choice1: Consumer spending plus investment plus government spending
choice2: Exports minus imports plus domestic consumption
choice3: Wages + profits + rents + interest earned in the economy
column15: Total output minus taxes plus subsidies

description: A price ceiling is set at $5 in a market where equilibrium is $8 and at $5 quantity supplied is 40 units and quantity demanded is 70 units. What is the size of the shortage?
explanation: Shortage = Qd - Qs at the ceiling price = 70 - 40 = 30 units.
hint: Shortage = Qd - Qs at the controlled price
choice1: 30 units
choice3: 40 units
column15: 70 units

description: A firm in the short run has fixed costs of $200, variable costs of $400 for producing 80 units. What is the average variable cost?
explanation: AVC = TVC / Q = $400 / 80 = $5 per unit.

description: The gains from trade according to the Ricardian model arise because:
explanation: By specializing in goods where their opportunity cost is lowest and trading countries can collectively produce more than if each tried to be self-sufficient.
choice1: Trade simply redistributes wealth between countries without creating new value
choice2: Specialization based on comparative advantage increases total production
choice3: The stronger country always benefits at the expense of the weaker
column15: Trade only benefits countries with large populations

description: In the Keynesian cross model if autonomous spending increases by $100 and the MPC is 0.6 equilibrium GDP increases by:
explanation: Multiplier = 1 / (1 - 0.6) = 2.5. Change in Y = 100 x 2.5 = $250.

description: The concept of consumer equilibrium states that utility is maximized when:
explanation: At the consumer optimum the last dollar spent on each good yields the same marginal utility. This ensures no reallocation can increase total utility.
choice1: The marginal utility per dollar is equal across all goods consumed
choice3: The marginal utility of every good equals zero
column15: Prices of all goods are equal

description: When a small country with a $3 domestic price joins free trade and the world price is $5, what happens?
explanation: The world price ($5) exceeds the domestic price ($3) so the country exports the good. Domestic producers gain and domestic consumers lose.
hint: Compare world price to domestic price to determine import vs. export
choice1: The country imports the good; consumers gain and producers lose
choice2: The price stays at $3 due to trade adjustment costs
choice3: Neither imports nor exports change
column15: The country exports the good; domestic producers gain and consumers lose

description: A firm's total revenue is $1,000 at a price of $10 and $1,100 at a price of $11. What can be concluded about the price elasticity of demand?
explanation: TR rises from $1
calculator: 100 as price rises from $10 to $11. When TR rises with price demand is inelastic (|PED| < 1).
verified: When TR and P move in same direction demand is inelastic
choice3: Demand is elastic (|PED| > 1)
column15: Demand is inelastic (|PED| < 1)

description: Automatic stabilizers reduce the size of the fiscal multiplier because:
explanation: Automatic stabilizers like income taxes and unemployment benefits mean that government spending and taxes adjust automatically offsetting some of the initial demand change and reducing the multiplier.
choice1: They increase government spending in every phase of the cycle
choice2: They prevent interest rates from changing
choice3: They offset some of the initial demand change reducing the effective multiplier
column15: They cause the central bank to raise rates automatically

description: What is the deadweight loss in a monopoly?
explanation: A monopoly restricts output below the competitive level to raise price. The deadweight loss is the value of transactions that would have occurred under competition but do not occur under monopoly.
choice1: Lost surplus from output not produced that would exist under perfect competition
choice3: The sum of consumer and producer surplus
column15: The difference between monopoly revenue and costs

description: If consumption is $6 trillion, investment is $2 trillion, government spending is $1.5 trillion, exports are $1 trillion, and imports are $1.2 trillion, what is GDP using the expenditure approach?
choice1: $11.7 trillion
choice3: $10.3 trillion
column15: $9.3 trillion

description: Open market operations involve:
explanation: Open market operations are the central bank's purchases or sales of government securities in the open market to change the money supply and influence interest rates.
choice1: The government selling goods and services directly
choice2: The central bank buying or selling government securities to influence the money supply
choice3: Banks lending to each other in the interbank market
column15: The treasury adjusting tax rates

description: At the minimum point of the long-run average cost curve a firm is said to be operating at:
explanation: The minimum point of the LRAC represents the most efficient scale of production. At this point the firm is at minimum efficient scale.
choice1: Diminishing returns
choice3: Minimum efficient scale (constant returns to scale)
column15: Diseconomies of scale

description: In a market for loanable funds if the government runs a large budget deficit and borrows heavily, the effect is:
explanation: Government borrowing increases the demand for loanable funds shifting the demand curve right. This raises the real interest rate and crowds out private investment.
choice1: The real interest rate rises and private investment falls (crowding out)
choice2: The real interest rate falls encouraging more investment
choice3: The supply of loanable funds increases matching demand
column15: The money supply automatically rises to fill the gap

description: If a factory producing steel also creates pollution the socially optimal level of steel output occurs where:
explanation: The social optimum accounts for all costs including the external cost of pollution. Output should be where social marginal cost (private MC + external cost) equals marginal benefit (demand).
choice1: Private marginal cost equals marginal revenue
choice3: Total social cost is minimized at any output level
column15: Social marginal cost (private MC + external cost) equals marginal benefit

description: Which best explains why the aggregate demand (AD) curve slopes downward?
explanation: AD slopes down because higher price levels reduce real wealth (wealth effect) raise interest rates (interest rate effect) and make domestic goods more expensive relative to foreign goods (exchange rate effect).
choice1: Higher prices cause firms to produce less
choice2: Higher prices reduce real purchasing power and raise interest rates making spending fall
choice3: Higher prices cause the money supply to contract
column15: Higher prices reduce government spending automatically

description: If the price of good X rises and a consumer buys more of good X, good X is most likely a:
explanation: If demand increases when price rises the income effect dominates the substitution effect. This can occur with inferior goods where the negative income effect (from reduced real income) is so large the consumer buys more - these are Giffen goods.
choice1: Normal good
choice3: Giffen good
column15: Complement to another good

description: The theory of comparative advantage suggests that global output is maximized when:
explanation: When each country specializes in goods where its opportunity cost is lowest and trades freely total global production expands beyond what would be achieved under autarky.
choice1: Each country specializes in goods where it has lowest opportunity cost and trades
choice2: Each country produces all of its own goods to ensure self-sufficiency
choice3: Only large developed economies engage in international trade
column15: Governments manage trade to ensure balanced bilateral trade
